title: Decide where workspace discovery executes
description:
The daemon owns the real workspace discovery implementation but is a library with no transport: morphir-daemon exposes Workspace::open and nothing over the wire. Decide the seam before implementing the browser.

## Context
Options: (a) implement the recorded glob and merge rules in TypeScript inside @morphir/ir or a new @morphir/workspace package; (b) wait for a daemon wire protocol and speak it from the hosts; (c) compile morphir-rust to WASM and call it - the extension seam the bootstrap spec anticipated. A secondary question rides along: whether the desktop host leads and the web host gets a reduced or delegated form, since discovery needs a filesystem.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision with rationale, captured in docs/specs, naming the seam and the web-host story.

title: Multi-project workspace and project browsing
description:
morphir-ui models a workspace as a single opened morphir-ir.json (WorkspaceState holds one OpenWorkspace). The recorded Morphir model is a workspace containing many member projects discovered by glob. Give the UI the multi-project hierarchy the specs and the daemon already define, so opening a real workspace root has somewhere to go.

## Context
Sources of truth in finos/morphir: docs/design/draft/daemon/workspace-config.md, docs/design/draft/daemon/projects.md, docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-specification.md. Real implementation in finos/morphir-rust: crates/morphir-daemon/src/workspace.rs. Evaluated against crates/morphir-live and found nothing worth porting - see GitHub issue #13.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a workspace root discovers its member projects per the recorded glob rules; each project shows its real lifecycle state; navigation runs workspace to project to module to definition into the existing explorer and insight views; opening a lone morphir-ir.json still works exactly as it does today.

title: CodeMirror 6 TOML view with two-way sync
description: Raw TOML editing in CodeMirror 6, kept in sync with the form view over the same document. Monaco was evaluated and rejected for this UI in the bootstrap spec.
acceptance_criteria: Edits in either view are reflected in the other; parse errors are surfaced without discarding the user's text.

title: Switch editing scope between user global, workspace and project
description: Choose which file an edit writes to, and make that choice visible. This is the UI face of the recorded precedence chain.
acceptance_criteria: The active scope is unambiguous in the UI, and writes land in the file the scope names.

title: Form view over morphir.toml
description: Svelte form surface over the modelled sections, with each field showing its effective value and provenance. Scoped styles and theme tokens only - no inline styles.
acceptance_criteria: Component tests cover editing, provenance display, and sections with no dedicated control degrading to a readable fallback.

title: Round-trip TOML edits without losing comments or unknown keys
description: Editing through the form view must not rewrite the document destructively. Comments, key order and unrecognized sections survive a form edit.
acceptance_criteria: Property or fixture tests assert that a form edit changes only the intended key and leaves everything else byte-identical where possible.

title: Model the morphir.toml section set
description:
Represent the sections the specification actually defines - morphir, workspace, project, frontend, ir, codegen, cache, logging, ui, sources, dependencies, dev-dependencies, extensions, tasks, workflows, toolchain - rather than a hand-picked subset. Unknown keys are preserved, not dropped.

## Context
morphir-live covered 7 of these and hand-wrote a form per section; that shape is not being carried forward.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip tests over real morphir.toml fixtures, including files using sections the UI has no form for.

title: Resolve effective configuration and provenance
description:
Implement the recorded precedence and DeepMerge rules and, for every effective value, record which scope it came from - user global, workspace, or project. Provenance is what makes this worth building instead of a text editor; morphir-live has none.

## Context
finos/morphir docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-merge-rules.md is normative: precedence order, DeepMerge semantics, provenance, environment variable mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Merge behaviour is tested against the normative examples; each resolved value exposes its source scope.

title: Surface project lifecycle state
description: Show each member project's state using the daemon's vocabulary - Unloaded, Loading, Ready, Stale, Error - rather than a boolean. Deliberately not morphir-live's is_active/Archived, which nothing backs.
acceptance_criteria: State is derived from real conditions (artifact present, artifact older than sources, load failed) and rendered with theme tokens; no invented states.

title: Keep the single-IR experience when a lone morphir-ir.json is opened
description: Multi-project support must not regress the current flow. Opening a single IR file behaves exactly as it does today.
acceptance_criteria: Existing workspace tests pass unchanged; a regression test covers the single-file path after the hierarchy lands.

title: Navigate workspace to project to module to definition
description: Extend the shell so the hierarchy is navigable and lands in the existing IR explorer and insight views, replacing the assumption of a single OpenWorkspace.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a project scopes the explorer to that project's IR; component tests cover navigation and scoping.

title: Discover member projects from a workspace root in the hosts
description: Extend the host WorkspaceService so opening a directory containing a workspace-mode morphir.toml discovers its member projects, and each project resolves its own configuration and IR artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop opens a real multi-project workspace fixture end to end; failures for individual members are isolated and surfaced rather than failing the whole open.

title: Model workspaces and member projects
description: Introduce workspace and member-project descriptors alongside the existing single-IR model, following the recorded [workspace] fields (root, output_dir, members, exclude, default_member) and [project] fields. Pure, host-independent, no Svelte or DOM.
acceptance_criteria: Types and glob member resolution are unit tested against fixture workspace layouts, including exclude patterns and default_member.

title: morphir.toml configuration editing with provenance
description:
Nothing in the ecosystem edits morphir.toml today - morphir-ui's settings surface edits application preferences under MORPHIR_HOME. Build a configuration editor with a form view and a raw TOML view over the same document, showing where every effective value came from.

## Context
Section set: finos/morphir docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-specification.md (14 sections). Precedence, DeepMerge and provenance: docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-merge-rules.md. Canonical model: finos/morphir-rust crates/morphir-common/src/config/model.rs. The dual form/TOML shape is the one idea taken from morphir-live; its partial config model, its form controls and its use of Monaco are not - see GitHub issue #13.
acceptance_criteria: Both views edit the same document and stay in sync; every effective value shows its source scope; edits round-trip without losing comments or unknown keys; the TOML view uses CodeMirror 6.
